output.question: Who are LinkedIn's main competitors?
output.answer: LinkedIn’s main competitors include Indeed, ZipRecruiter and Glassdoor, particularly in U.S. job search and recruiting. ([sensortower.com](https://sensortower.com/blog/your-job-depends-on-it-how-four-top-career-sites-competing-for-users-mobile-app-web)) Other important competitors include Monster, Dice for technology recruiting, Handshake for college recruiting, and Naukri.com in India. ([g2.com](https://www.g2.com/products/linkedin-job-search/competitors/alternatives)) The competitive set depends on the service: LinkedIn also competes in professional networking, learning, advertising and sales intelligence, so job platforms are not substitutes for its entire business. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/investor/reports/ar26/))

key_facts.fact: Indeed, Glassdoor and ZipRecruiter are prominent U.S. competitors: Sensor Tower analyzed them alongside LinkedIn as four top job and career websites.
G2 lists Monster, Dice, Handshake and Naukri.com among alternatives to LinkedIn Job Search.
G2 describes Dice as focused on technology professionals, Handshake as a college career network, and Naukri.com as an Indian employment platform.
Microsoft's annual report identifies LinkedIn competition across professional networks, recruiting and HR services, job boards, learning, advertising, lead generation and customer intelligence.

passages.quote: We analyzed four of the top job and career websites, LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, and ZipRecruiter
Handshake is the college career network of the future
LinkedIn faces competition from online professional networks; recruiting, talent management, and human resource services companies; job boards;

caveats: This is a synthesis of prominent competitors, not an official ranked list or a market-share ranking.
The leading competitors vary by geography and by LinkedIn product; the strongest evidence for Indeed, ZipRecruiter and Glassdoor here concerns U.S. job search and recruiting.
G2's alternatives page is dynamic and does not display a publication date; its facts are dated to the research date.
The opened Microsoft annual report identifies the reporting year but does not establish an exact publication date.
